prompt: To MOVE a halogen from one carbon to an adjacent one (e.g., 2-bromopentane → 3-bromopentane), what strategy works?

options.label: E2 to the alkene (strong base), then add HBr back (with/without peroxides) at the new carbon
SN1 ionization to a cation that rearranges, then Br⁻ attacks the rearranged carbocation
LiAlH₄ reduces the C-Br bond; the hydride ends up adjacent, pushing Br to the new position
Not possible — halogens can't be migrated between carbons without changing the carbon skeleton

explanation: The classic eliminate-then-add strategy: E2 removes HBr to form the alkene (losing the halogen entirely), then HBr addition puts it on a different C. Choice of Markovnikov vs anti-Markovnikov (peroxides or not) controls which C gets the Br. SN1 rearrangements are possible but unreliable.
